newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares dip as investors pause to introspect.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares dip as investors pause to introspect.

text.p: Egyptian share prices dipped on Monday as investors stopped helter-skelter trading to take a long, hard look at the market, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its overall index slipped 0.85 percent or 3.38 points to 395.2 on below-par turnover of 59.91 million pounds ($17.62 million).
"It was a quiet day which is good because the market needs people to look at things intellectually," said Ahmed el-Helw, managing director of Intercapital brokerage.
"Investors have to stop rushing all the way to the left and then all the way to the right. The market needs time to be reconsidered," he added.
Share prices have zig-zagged between record highs and profit taking driven lows since last month's rally.
Despite the slowed activity, all eyes were on the blue-chip cement sector which brokers said had the most potential.
"It's solid, its more than stable and rising slowly but surely. Volume is huge and growth in earnings is an average 32 percent. Cements are the most attractive," Helw said.

Amriyah Cement topped the day's trading with 8.2 million pounds of turnover but ended 1.65 pounds lower at 86.35 despite announcing a 21 percent increase in profits for the first half of the 1996/7 financial year.
Suez Cement also featured strongly but fell 2.0 pounds to 72.00. Egyptian Portland Tora Cement was the sector's only gainer, rising 1.50 to 97 in average trade.
Milling firms were conspicuously absent among the most actively traded shares and many ended lower as the introspective investors kept out of the sector.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills, the most active share, fell 1.57 to 104.45 in thin volume but related firm General Silos and Storage rose 0.01 to 111 in hearty turnover of 3.1 million pounds.

Fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial was still rising in heavy volume on Monday as the market still buzzed with rumours that it would buy out a competitor. Shares gained 3.0 pounds to 209 in 6.22 million pounds of trading.

The housing sector, which helped build up the market's dizzying heights, saw a slight correction with main player Heliopolis Housing and Development shedding 19 pounds to 435. Medinet Nasr Housing and Development gained 6.0 pounds to 488 but brokers predicted it would also fall soon.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 643.75 from 656.16 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped slightly to 264.6 points from 265.00.
Out of the 86 shares traded, 30 gained, 33 lost and 23 ended the day unchanged.
